title: A thousand times the words
hook: Add 990 words to a letter tree. Does looking up "cat" get slower?

knows: search trees compare a whole word at each node (lopsided-tree)
doesNotKnow: a tree that branches on letters instead of comparing whole words
that lookup cost follows the word's length

misconception: Looking up a word gets slower as the dictionary grows.
objective: The learner can explain that in a letter tree each step picks the next letter, so looking up a word costs its length (3 steps for cat) however many words the tree holds.

claims.text: Looking up "cat" takes 3 steps in a letter tree of 10 words and 3 steps in a letter tree of 1,000 words.
claims.source: Builder's node script (2026-10-14): built a letter tree from the 10 starting words (cat car cap dog dot sun sea art ant bat), then from the 1,000-word list (the same 10 plus 990 seeded invented strings, mulberry32 seed 1000, lengths 3 to 8, all distinct). Walking c, a, t reaches an end-of-word mark in both: 3 steps and 3 steps. The same script confirms steps = length for all 1,000 words. The seed was not searched for; it was the first one tried. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Own node rebuild (scratchpad fc1/trie.mjs, kit mulberry32 seed 1000, randInt 3..8): 1,000 distinct words; walking c,a,t ends on an end-of-word mark at depth 3 in the 10-word and the 1,000-word tree; steps = length for all 1,000 words.

claims.text: The 990 added words are invented letter strings of 3 to 8 letters, not a real dictionary; the stage's grey counts (for example 48 words start with c) are counted from that list.
claims.source: Generator in Demo.tsx (mulberry32 seed 1000, randInt length 3..8, letters a..z, duplicates and the 10 starters skipped until 1,000 words). Builder's node reimplementation: 1,000 distinct words; first-letter counts a 44, b 40, c 48, d 51, s 41 and so on, summing to 1,000. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Same script: 990 added strings, lengths 3 to 8, letters a-z; first-letter counts c 48, d 51, s 41, a 44, b 40 ..., summing to 1,000; the stage prints FIRST[ch] from that same list.

claims.text: In a letter tree each step follows the next letter of the word, so the number of steps equals the word's length, however many words the tree holds (assuming a fixed alphabet and constant-time choice of child).
claims.source: A word of length L has one node per prefix, so a lookup visits L nodes. Choosing the child by letter is one array or map access for a fixed alphabet (26 letters). Knuth, TAOCP Vol. 3, 6.3 (digital searching). Reveal text: 'the cost is the length of the word, not how many words the tree holds'. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Derivation: a successful lookup of a length-L word visits one node per prefix, L steps, with one child choice per step (constant for a fixed 26-letter alphabet); the number of stored words never enters. Knuth TAOCP Vol. 3 (2nd ed.) 6.3 digital searching. Node check: steps = length for all 1,000 words.

claims.text: The letter tree (trie) was described by Fredkin in 1960.
claims.source: E. Fredkin, 'Trie memory', Communications of the ACM 3(9), 1960. Not shown to the learner on the stage; recorded for the brief. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Web search (Crossref DOI 10.1145/367390.367400; NIST DADS 'trie'; Wikipedia 'Trie'): E. Fredkin, 'Trie memory', CACM 3(9):490-499, Sept 1960. Note: de la Briandais (1959) described the structure independently; 'described by Fredkin' is still true.

claims.text: One step means following one letter down the tree.
claims.source: Counting convention stated on the stage: the model line 'One step = follow one letter down the tree.' It ignores the cost of picking the child (see c3). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Convention stated on the stage model line, 'One step = follow one letter down the tree.'; the readout counts exactly the letters walked.

claims.text: The 990 new words grew branches beside the walked path; the path to cat stayed three hops long.
claims.source: Same script as c1: the cat node is at depth 3 in both trees; the 990 words add nodes elsewhere (the c branch alone holds 48 words in the 1,000-word list, 5 of them starting ca). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Same script: cat is at depth 3 in both trees; c branch 48 words, 5 starting 'ca' (cat, car, cap, cavblpcu, cacruudt); the added words create nodes off the c-a-t path.

recall.question: A letter tree holds 50,000 words. About how many steps does it take to look up a 6-letter word in it?
recall.why: Each step follows the next letter, so a 6-letter word takes 6 steps whatever the tree holds. About 16 is the number of halvings of 50,000, which is binary search, not a letter tree.
